ecological_definition: Ecological succession: the process by which an ecosystem gradually recovers through a series of stages after a disturbance, analogous to secondary succession following a forest fire
core_case: Wukong was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain for 500 years; Flower Fruit Mountain went from ‘monkey-troop peak’ to ‘harassed by hunters’ and back to ‘recovery’ — a complete history of secondary succession

succession_stages.name: Peak · Great Sage Equal to Heaven era
succession_stages.ecological_description: Flower Fruit Mountain, a blessed land · Water Curtain Cave, a paradise · monkeys thriving · no natural enemies · extremely high biodiversity
succession_stages.keystone_species: Sun Wukong (Great Sage Equal to Heaven)

succession_stages.name: Disturbance · Havoc in Heaven
succession_stages.year_range: The year of Havoc in Heaven
succession_stages.ecological_description: Wukong rebelled against the Celestial Court · Flower Fruit Mountain was burned by heavenly troops · the ‘Seven Great Sages’ alliance dissolved · the first major disturbance
succession_stages.disturbance_event: Heavenly troops attacked with fire · burned most of Flower Fruit Mountain

succession_stages.name: Collapse · 500 years under Five Elements Mountain · hunter slaughter
succession_stages.year_range: During the 500 years under Five Elements Mountain
succession_stages.ecological_description: Wukong was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain · the troop lost its leader · hunters frequently raided · ‘setting fires + netting and arrows’ · the monkey troop plunged from 47,000 to 1,300 · a 97% decline
succession_stages.disturbance_event: Hunters slaughtered relentlessly · burning + arrows + netting

succession_stages.name: Remnant · Wukong returns · clearing the hunters
succession_stages.year_range: 1st year after release from Five Elements Mountain
succession_stages.ecological_description: Wukong returned to Flower Fruit Mountain · greeted by ‘over a thousand monkeys’ · cleared out 1,000+ hunters · rebuilt Water Curtain Cave · restored order

succession_stages.name: Recovery · on the pilgrimage · Wukong’s occasional returns
succession_stages.ecological_description: Wukong occasionally returned to Flower Fruit Mountain · the troop was recovering · but was still harassed in his absence · not yet fully restored

succession_stages.name: Buddhahood · the Victorious Fighting Buddha returns
succession_stages.ecological_description: Wukong became the Victorious Fighting Buddha · occasionally returned to Flower Fruit Mountain · the troop recovered to 1/6 of its peak · the ecosystem stabilized

succession_insights: Flower Fruit Mountain underwent a complete secondary succession: peak → disturbance → collapse → remnant → recovery → buddhahood
The loss of the keystone species (Sun Wukong) was the root cause of the collapse · not the hunters themselves
Over 500 years the troop plunged from 47,000 to 1,300 · a 97.2% decline · ecological collapse
The hunter slaughter was essentially a chain reaction after keystone loss · not an independent disturbance
Slow recovery: 14+ years to go from 1,300 to 8,000 · still not back to the peak
After buddhahood the troop recovered to 8,000 · only 17% of the peak · ecological recovery is a long road

modern_parallel.yellowstone_wolves: Yellowstone wolf reintroduction: keystone loss caused ecological collapse · recovery after reintroduction
modern_parallel.forest_fire_succession: Secondary succession after a forest fire: pioneer species → intermediate species → climax community
modern_parallel.island_ecology: Island ecology: Flower Fruit Mountain resembles an isolated island · keystone loss hits even harder
modern_parallel.wukong_as_keystone: Wukong is Flower Fruit Mountain’s keystone species · equivalent to Yellowstone’s wolves
